methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.

actual_scope: On one equal-weight path of bandwidth 2, what is the Schur half-bandwidth after one interior is deleted and the survivors stay in increasing index?
scope_change_reason: The length-9 arc census has no off-diagonal pair left. The named next step is one interior in the boundary order stated by GAUSSIAN.md.
bottleneck_link: GAUSSIAN.md uses a Schur matrix of bandwidth O(W) in boundary order. On this path the half-bandwidth is 3 for interiors of length 2, 4, and 6, while the original-index span of the same entry grows from 5 to 9.
stop_rule: Stop once these three width-2 interiors are measured. Do not start a width-3 path or a truncated Gaussian row.
evidence: research/boundary-order-width2 records half-bandwidth 3 and corner entries -1/504, -1/1664, and -121/887692.
author: jwr
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from the Cursor coding agent in the Schur identities, checker and writeup.

open_questions.question: On the same equal-weight path at width 3, is the boundary-order half-bandwidth 5 for one interior of length 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Width 2 attains 2W-1. A third width would show whether that constant is special to W=2.
open_questions.first_step: Delete indices 4 through 7 on a width-3 path with four vertices of padding on each side, and measure the survivor half-bandwidth.

open_questions.question: Does one truncated Gaussian row, with the stated boundary order, have Schur half-bandwidth O(W)?

open_questions.first_step: Pin one finite Gaussian section, one interior, and the survivor order, then measure the Schur half-bandwidth.
